narrative.title: Longest Unbroken Session Chain in a Session Log
narrative.scenario: An analytics store keeps session numbers from many tenants in one unsorted table, and repeated numbers appear when a session is retried. The growth team wants the longest chain of back-to-back session numbers, where the chain does not need to be contiguous in the table. Report the length of that chain.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers, the session numbers in arbitrary order.
narrative.outputFormat: The length of the longest run of consecutive integers present in nums, ignoring duplicates.

testCases.explanation: The numbers 1,2,3,4 form an unbroken chain of four, ignoring their scrambled positions.
Duplicated 0 does not extend the chain, but 0 through 8 are all present for a length of 9.

hintLevels: Level 1: Sorting solves it but costs O(n log n); a hash set answers membership questions in constant expected time instead.
Level 2: Put every value into a set, then only start counting from values whose predecessor is absent - those are chain heads.
Level 3: Always expand from the head rather than from every element, otherwise the inner walk repeats the same chain and degrades to quadratic time.
